import math
capitals = {
  "Brunei": (4.89028,114.94222),
  "Cambodia": (11.55,104.917),
  "Indonesia": (-0.456,117.116),  # using Nusantara coords
  "Laos": (17.98,102.63),
  "Malaysia": (3.14778,101.69528),
  "Myanmar": (19.763,96.0785),
  "Philippines": (14.5995,120.9842),
  "Singapore": (1.3521,103.8198),
  "Thailand": (13.7563,100.5018),
  "Vietnam": (21.0278,105.8342)
}
R=6371
pairs=[]
keys=list(capitals.keys())
for i in range(len(keys)):
    for j in range(i+1,len(keys)):
        (lat1,lon1)=capitals[keys[i]]
        (lat2,lon2)=capitals[keys[j]]
        phi1=math.radians(lat1); phi2=math.radians(lat2)
        dphi=math.radians(lat2-lat1)
        dlambda=math.radians(lon2-lon1)
        a=math.sin(dphi/2)**2 + math.cos(phi1)*math.cos(phi2)*math.sin(dlambda/2)**2
        d=2*R*math.asin(math.sqrt(a))
        pairs.append(((keys[i],keys[j]), d))
# sort by distance desc
pairs.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
print(pairs[:5])

This failure to ask for clarification on incomplete/transitioning information (FM-2.2) led to using the wrong capital city coordinates in the dataset, which skewed the subsequent distance calculation and produced the incorrect final pair.
